# Dragonfly.eco

> > A curated exploration of eco-fiction and climate literature, featuring book databases, author spotlights, and environmental storytelling resources.

Created and maintained by Mary Woodbury, Dragonfly.eco serves as a comprehensive volunteer resource for eco-fiction (environmental literature) and cli-fi (climate fiction), connecting readers with books that explore humanity's relationship with nature and climate change. The site includes extensive databases, author interviews, and educational resources about environmental literature.

- eco-fiction
- climate-fiction (cli-fi)

## Getting Started

- [Dragonfly: An exploration of eco-fiction](https://dragonfly.eco): Homepage featuring eco-fiction spotlights, indie author series, and climate lit
- [About Dragonfly.eco](https://dragonfly.eco/about): About page by curator Mary Woodbury; eco-fiction database and mission
- [What is Eco-fiction?](https://dragonfly.eco/eco-fiction): Comprehensive guide defining eco-fiction, citing Jim Dwyer and Lawrence Buell
- [Site Tour Guide](https://dragonfly.eco/navigating-site): Site navigation guide and tour of Dragonfly.eco features and structure

## Resources & Reference

- [News Links](https://dragonfly.eco/news): Curated collection of news articles about eco-themes in literature
- [Dragonflies & Climate](https://dragonfly.eco/dragonflies): Site origin story, .eco domain adoption, and dragonfly climate symbolism

## Author Features & Writing Process

- [Climate Novelists Writing Process Blog Tour](https://dragonfly.eco/climate-novelists-writing-process-blog-tour): Blog tour inviting climate fiction authors to share their writing process
- [Peter Romilly's Writing Process](https://dragonfly.eco/climate-novelists-writing-process-blog-tour/peter-romillys-writing-process-blog-tour): Peter Romilly discusses Cli-Fidelity and fracking novel Frack That
